name: Hot Honey Chicken and Broccoli Bowls
intro_html: Sweet, a little spicy, and shockingly lean. Chicken breast and tender broccoli over rice, all glazed in hot honey for a sweet-heat kick that makes leftovers something to look forward to. At 31 grams of protein and only 3 grams of fat for around a dollar fifteen, this one earns a permanent spot in the rotation.
ingredients_display: Boneless skinless chicken breast (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb (1587 g, raw)
cost_note_html: Real Walmart and Sam's Club prices (2026). They still swing by region and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Jasmine rice, ~1.6 lb (~$1.45/lb): ~$2.24. Buy the big bag (lasts many batches).
Hot honey, ~7 tbsp (of a ~$3.98 bottle): ~$1.75. Buy 1 bottle (lasts several batches).
Batch total: about $16.24 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.16 per bowl.

True shopping cost: about $17.99 across 14 servings, roughly $1.29 per bowl. This is what you actually pay when you buy whole packages, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar, and you will have a little left over for next time. Pantry staples like rice, seasoning, and long-lasting sauces are counted at what this batch actually uses, because one package covers several batches.
cost_closing_html: About $1.16 a bowl for a lean, crave-worthy dinner that would run $12 or more at a fast-casual spot.
shop_smart: Chicken on sale, frozen, is the move. Buy a big pack when the price drops and freeze it in two-pound bags.
A little hot honey goes far. One bottle glazes several batches, so the per-serving cost stays tiny even though it feels like a treat.
Frozen broccoli is cheaper than fresh, lasts for months, and cooks right from the bag.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice. Three and a half cups dry jasmine with water per the package, then set aside.
Cube the chicken and cook in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it reaches 165F inside.
Steam or microwave the broccoli until bright and tender.
Turn the heat to low, drizzle the hot honey over the chicken, and toss until glazed.
Combine the rice, hot honey chicken, and broccoli in your big pot and stir.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container. Every bowl lands near 357 calories and 31 grams of protein at just 3 grams of fat.
upsell_html: Lean, crave-worthy dinners for about $1.16 a bowl. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.
